Note::all¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::all() const

Require Every Boolean Lane¶

all() reduces an entire Bool Note to one rank-zero Bool Note. The result is true only when every lane of the receiver is true. There is no axis parameter: rank and shape determine how many lanes are visited, but all axes participate in this reduction.

The result deliberately remains a Note. That keeps a predicate pipeline inside the closed Note type: compose cellwise conditions first, reduce them, then either keep the scalar Note for further Note operations or cross the host boundary with bool_item() when a C++ bool is required.

all() accepts only a defined Bool Note. Text that happens to contain "true", and integers that happen to be zero or one, are not coerced. Build a Bool Note directly or obtain one from a predicate, comparison, or Boolean operator.

Reduction Contract¶

Receiver

Result

every lane is true

scalar Bool Note containing true

at least one lane is false

scalar Bool Note containing false

scalar Bool Note

the same truth value in a newly allocated scalar Note

empty Bool Note of any shape

scalar true

Text, Bytes, Int64, or Float64 Note

error

undefined Note

error

The empty result is true because true is the identity for conjunction. This makes all() compositional: appending no additional conditions cannot turn a previously valid conjunction into a failure. It also means that callers whose domain requires at least one observation must test empty() separately.

The implementation scans contiguous one-byte Boolean lanes and can stop at the first false. Runtime is O(k) in the worst case for k = numel(), with no dependence on the receiver’s rank. The only result allocation is one Boolean lane plus scalar metadata; text arenas are never inspected.

Example 1: All Lanes Pass¶

const auto checks = pluss::note::make({true, true});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(checks.all()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

Example 2: One Failure Is Enough¶

const auto checks = pluss::note::make({true, false});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(checks.all()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
false

The returned shape is [], not [1]: reduction produces a scalar even when the receiver is a vector.

Example 3: Reduce A Higher-Rank Predicate¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Ada", "Grace", "Linus", "Alan"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto nonempty = values.lengths_chars() > pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{0});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(nonempty) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(nonempty.all()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, dtype=Bool)
[
  [true, true], 
  [true, true]
]
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

all() does not reduce each row separately. It consumes all four matrix lanes. Use shape operations to isolate a subset before reducing when the question concerns only part of a Note.

Example 4: Compose Conditions Before Reducing¶

const auto names = pluss::note::make({"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"});
const auto acceptable = names.contains("a") |
                        (names.lengths_chars() >=
                         pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{5}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(acceptable) << '\n';
std::cout << "all acceptable=" << std::boolalpha
          << acceptable.all().bool_item() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Bool)
[true, true, true]
all acceptable=true

The first line stays in Note space. bool_item() is used only for the final host control-flow value.

Example 5: Scalar Input¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make(false).all()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
false

Scalar reduction still returns a fresh scalar Bool Note rather than a native bool.

Example 6: Empty Conjunction¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{0, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(empty.all()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, dtype=Bool)
true

The original empty shape does not survive a full reduction; only the scalar identity does.

Example 7: Invalid Receivers Reject¶

try { (void)pluss::note::make({"true", "false"}).all(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "all Text: rejected\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::Note::undefined().all(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "all undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

all Text: rejected
all undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • any: ask whether at least one Boolean lane passes.

  • operators: construct and combine Bool Notes with comparisons and &, |, ^, and ~.

  • empty: distinguish an empty domain from a nonempty all-true domain when the application requires observations.
